topic.title: Distribution Estimation and Robust Statistical Limits
topic.overview: This topic asks how accurately a probability distribution, its mean, or one of its properties can be estimated from finite data. Sparse observations, infinite support, heavy tails, and contamination create different limits. The represented work combines algorithms with upper and lower bounds that clarify which assumptions make estimation possible.
topic.whyItMatters: A precise estimate of the wrong quantity or an unsupported uniform guarantee can be misleading. Data-dependent bounds and explicit contamination models help connect theoretical accuracy to what the observed sample actually reveals.
topic.evolution: Early representatives study uniform convergence and approximation. Later work estimates unseen mass and distributional properties, followed by heavy-tailed regression and assumption-light discrete-distribution learning. Recent mean-shift contamination analysis exploits structure that differs from arbitrary replacement noise. These models must remain distinct: robustness under one corruption mechanism does not automatically transfer to another.
openQuestions: Which observable diagnostics can justify a data-dependent estimation guarantee?
How much distributional structure is needed to recover information hidden by contamination?
